title: Localizing an enriched categorical mapping cylinder retracts to its target
statement:
Use small simplicial categories, Dwyer--Kan equivalences, and the fixed strict interval-attachment model $\Gamma(D,V)$ of [lem-coef-simplicial-arrow-attachment-localization], in fixed containing universes. Let $f:C\to D$ be any simplicial functor between small simplicial categories. Define $M_f$ to have the disjoint union of their object sets. Its mapping simplicial sets within the two summands are $C(x,y)$ and $D(x,y)$, respectively. For $x\in C$ and $y\in D$ put $M_f(x,y)=D(fx,y)$; for $x\in D$ and $y\in C$ put $M_f(x,y)=\varnothing$. 
Composition within a summand is its composition; for a cross arrow use $f$ on the $C$-arrow and composition in $D$. Let $j:M_f\to D$ send $x\in C$ to $fx$, act as the identity on $D$, and use $f$ on $C$-mapping sets and the identity on cross mapping sets. Let $V$ be any small set of labelled vertex arrows in $M_f$ such that $j(v)$ is an identity for every $v\in V$, and such that, for every $x\in C$, the cross arrow $x\to fx$ represented by $1_{fx}$ occurs in $V$. Then the identity-collapse extension
$$\bar j:\Gamma(M_f,V)\longrightarrow D$$
is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. Neither $f$ nor the mapping simplicial sets of $C,D$ are assumed cofibrant or Kan. Empty $C$ and empty $D$ are allowed whenever the functor $f$ exists.
